evidence: Home page grid shows 6 templates each with title, author (e.g. Sarah Chen), description text visible in card.
Clicking 'Use Template' on Professional Resume opened preview.panel dialog with template details and a 'Fill Template' form tab listing 14 fields.

All 14 fields (name, title, email, phone, summary, company, position, startDate, endDate, responsibilities, degree, school, graduationYear, skills) accepted typed values via browser_fill_form; semantic_observe confirmed values stored.
After filling all fields with valid values, Preview Result tab rendered a document with all values substituted (Jane Doe, Software Engineer, jane.doe@example.com, Acme Corp, etc.).
Each card in templates.grid shows category badge (Resume), scenario badge (Business), title, description, author, usage count, and updated date.

Professional Resume preview rendered as Markdown: h1 name heading, bold job title, separator, h2 section headings, emphasis for date range, all placeholders replaced with entered values, no raw placeholder tokens remained.
Clicking Copy to Clipboard button changed its label/state to 'Copied!' providing visible success feedback.

actual: Entering 'not-an-email' as the Email* value (a field with a declared email format) did not block the Preview Result tab or prevent generation; preview.result rendered 'Jane Doe Software Engineer | not-an-email | ...' with the invalid string embedded, instead of rejecting the value or keeping the preview unavailable.

issue: Preview becomes available with an invalid (non-blank but malformed) required field value
actual: With Email set to the invalid value 'not-an-email' (all other required fields non-blank), the Preview Result tab became enabled and generated content immediately, rather than remaining unavailable until the value was valid. Blank-required-field case correctly kept the tab disabled, but validity was not enforced.

evidence: With all fields blank, preview.missing-fields observable listed 'Please fill in: Full Name, Job Title, Email, Professional Summary, Company Name, Position, Start Date, Responsibilities, Degree, School, Graduation Year, Skills' and the Preview Result tab was disabled (click timed out as not-enabled).

Category filter (Meeting Minutes) narrowed to 1 of 6; scenario filter (Academic) narrowed to 1 of 6 (Academic Research Summary); Alphabetical sort reordered grid to Academic Research Summary, Meeting Minutes, Professional Email, Professional Resume, Project Proposal, Weekly Status Report. Result count updated each time.

actual: Typing 'Resme' (single-letter-deletion typo of 'Resume') and 'Meetign' (transposition typo of 'Meeting') both returned 'Showing 0 of 6 templates' with 'No templates found' and no suggestions, instead of matching Professional Resume / Meeting Minutes.

evidence: Favoriting Professional Resume set header.favorites.count to 1 and toggling header.favorites (Favorites-only) filter showed 'Showing 1 of 6 templates' with only Professional Resume listed.

While favorites-only filter was on, typing 'Resume' in search kept result at 'Showing 1 of 6 templates' (matching favorited item) and applying category=Resume filter also correctly kept the single favorited match.

Typing 'Me' (2 chars) populated search.suggestions collection with 5 items (Professional Resume, Full Name, Company Name, Your Name, Department); clicking the 'Professional Resume' suggestion filled the search box with 'Professional Resume' and narrowed results to 'Showing 1 of 6 templates'.

All filter/sort/search/favorites interactions (category, scenario, sort, favorites-only, search) updated filters.result-count and templates.grid content immediately in the same semantic_snapshot call with no page navigation/reload performed.
Toggling favorite on Professional Resume immediately changed toggle state to 'on', header.favorites.count changed from absent/0 to '1', and header.favorites label updated to 'Favorites 1'.

issue: Custom template submission accepted with unmapped placeholder; generated preview contains unresolved placeholder
actual: Submitted a custom template whose content included {{hiringManager}} with no corresponding declared field (only 'name' and 'company' fields were defined). Submission succeeded (library went from 6 to 7 templates) instead of being rejected. Using the template and filling name/company, the generated preview literally showed 'Dear {{hiringManager}},' — an unresolved placeholder — instead of blocking submission or resolving it.

evidence: Submit dialog accepted title, author, description, category (Other), scenario (Business), Markdown content, and two defined fields (Name, Company); Submit Template action succeeded and closed the dialog.

After submission, templates.grid grew from 6 to 7 items including 'Simple Cover Letter'; clicking its Use Template opened a fill form with Name/Company fields, values were entered, and Preview Result rendered generated content.

Immediately after clicking Submit Template (no navigation/reload), filters.result-count changed from 'Showing 6 of 6 templates' to 'Showing 7 of 7 templates' and the new card appeared in templates.grid within the same snapshot call.

issue: Duplicate field labels are silently accepted, not rejected or disambiguated
actual: Adding two custom-template fields both labeled 'Recipient' resulted in two entries in submit.fields both with id/key 'recipient' and label 'Recipient' — no error, warning, or automatic disambiguation (e.g. renaming to 'Recipient 2') occurred; the Add Field action succeeded both times.

evidence: Submitting with all text fields blank kept the dialog open and did not add a template (count stayed 'Showing 6 of 6'). Separately, submitting title/author/description/content filled but zero fields defined also failed to submit (count stayed 'Showing 7 of 7', dialog remained open).

A custom plain-text template (Markdown toggle off) with content 'Note for {{recipient}}: This is a *plain* # text message, not markdown.' rendered in preview.result as literal unformatted text 'Note for Team: This is a *plain* # text message, not markdown.' — asterisks and # were preserved as plain characters, not rendered as Markdown emphasis/heading. Combined with the earlier Professional Resume Markdown case (FT-8), both plain-text and Markdown rendering behave as expected content-wise.

issue: Markdown-structural characters (#, *, -) in field values are not rejected/neutralized, allowing them to alter generated Markdown formatting
actual: The app does block characters < > { } [ ] \\ | ` with error 'Special characters like < > { } [ ] \\ | ` are not allowed' (e.g. entering '' in Full Name triggered this validation). However, entering '# Injected Heading\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Bold Injected**' (using only #, *, - which are not in the blocked set) was accepted with no error, and the generated Markdown preview rendered it as an actual h1 heading containing raw '# Injected Heading ---' text plus a bold Bold Injected element inside the name heading, and elsewhere the Start Date value '2020' was wrapped in literal asterisks '*2020 - *' — demonstrating the user-entered Markdown syntax altered the document structure instead of being neutralized/escaped.

evidence: After navigating to http://localhost:6089/ again (full reload), templates.grid still showed 8 templates including the custom 'Plain Text Note' and 'Simple Cover Letter', header.favorites.count remained '1', and Professional Resume's favorite toggle state remained 'on'.
